caption: The drawing consists of two main groups of people positioned in an outdoor scene. On the left side, a group of men are dressed in colonial-style European clothing, including coats, waistcoats, breeches, stockings, and tricorn hats. Some have long hair or wigs, and most are standing or gesturing toward the figures on the right. In the center foreground, a man kneels, with his left arm extended toward another group. To the right, there is a group of Indigenous people, some of whom are partially clothed or topless. These figures have distinctive hairstyles, adornments, and blankets or cloths draped around their waists or shoulders. Among them are women, men, and children, some of whom are engaged in conversation or interacting with the newcomers. Behind both groups, there are several colonial-style two- and three-story buildings with pitched roofs, chimneys, and windows visible, accompanied by tall trees and foliage. In the background, to the far left, a body of water with a sailing ship is visible. The drawing is done in monochrome, primarily rendered in sepia or brown ink, with detailed linework and shading. At the bottom right corner, the name "MICHAEL" and "PERKY" are written, along with “1961.”
title: Printed Historical Textile
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
